propositions: Autodeploy recreates the review-bot container mid-review without draining in-flight work, killing active code reviews before they can vote, causing the LLM-Review gate to live-lock during landing bursts when deploy intervals are shorter than review duration.

The bot's lifespan drain protects webhook-queued reviews via queue.join(), but not reconciler-retried reviews which await review_and_vote inline and are cancelled within SHUTDOWN_CANCEL_SECONDS, making the retry path the unprotected self-heal mechanism.

A fully live-locked gate with zero votes leaves every health signal green (docker inspect running, VOTER_ERROR silent, CloudWatch alarms OK) because killed reviews emit no error, creating a blind spot in the fail-closed voter alarm that eb6e's safety net depends on.

Autodeploy was changed to DEFER recreation when the bot reports in-flight reviews rather than recreating immediately, with a bound of DEPLOY_DEFER_MAX=1800s keyed to the deferral episode not the SHA, preventing timer reset during bursts.

The defer signal requires adding an in_flight field to the existing /health endpoint, and deferral is logged via AUTODEPLOY_DEFERRED and AUTODEPLOY_REVIEW_INTERRUPT tokens to an observable CloudWatch alarm rebar-autodeploy-review-interrupts.

A landing burst with six deploys arriving while one review runs now results in zero recreations during the burst and exactly one compose-build at the newest tip, with the interrupt failure mode now alarmed rather than silent.
